newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac mulls offers for unit - report.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac mulls offers for unit - report.

text.p: British building group Tarmac Plc is considering two offers for its plant hire business Castle Plant Services, The Times said on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted Tarmac chief executive Neville Simms as saying Castle would be sold if the price was right. It gave no details of the reported bidders.
Castle includes the plant hire business acquired as part of last year's asset swap with George Wimpey Plc, The Times said.
Tarmac on Tuesday reported a stronger than expected rise in 1996 underlying pretax profits to 75.5 million stg ($122.8 million).
It took a one-off charge of 65 million stg related to its integration of the former Wimpey minerals and construction businesses gained in exchange for Tarmac's housing unit.
